title: Band-Pass Filter - Band 8 (900 MHz) for Millimeter-Wave Beamforming
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Elena Vasquez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Band-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 8 (900 MHz) for Millimeter-Wave Beamforming. The filter is designed on PZT on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 5547.8 MHz and bandwidth of 373.2 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Millimeter-Wave Beamforming module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Band-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 8 (900 MHz)
- Application: Millimeter-Wave Beamforming
- Substrate: PZT on Si
- Package: LGA (Land Grid Array)
- Design Tool: Ansys HFSS 2024R1
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Band-Pass Filter design targeting Band 8 (900 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       5547.8 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       373.2 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.3 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 17.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 32.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 30.0 dB
Q Factor:               7963
Temperature Coefficient:-29.0 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.1 x 1.0 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   11
Electrode Material:     W
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Ansys HFSS 2024R1 and load the Band-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: PZT on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 5547.8 MHz, BW 373.2 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.3 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (LGA (Land Grid Array)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, PZT on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNB40.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 16643 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.3 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 17.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 560 MHz offset >= 32.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 4 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 20.1 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +32 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 89%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-05-24
Devices Tested:         18
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.03 dB
Return Loss (meas):     18.8 dB
Rejection (meas):       35.0 dB
Isolation (meas):       35.2 dB
Q Factor (meas):        7963
Group Delay Variation:  2.9 ns
Power Handling:         +29 dBm
Die Yield:              90.3%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Band-Pass Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 8 (900 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
